rows.author: G101;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 9711, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION ACT\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to supplement the FDA law (RA9711) by having a single unit dedicated to the screening, evaluation and processing of technical documents and other regulatory requirements for the traditional medicine (TM) and herbal supplement (HS) products.
Proposes to create the CENTER FOR TRADITIONAL AND ALTERNATIVE MEDICINE exclusively devoted for these group of products under the FDA, which will streamline and expedite registration procedures to facilitate the release of product registration certificates.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2018-08-08

rows.author: G110;G111;G109;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING REGIONAL JAILS UNDER THE BUREAU OF CORRECTIONS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the worsened overcrowding/overcapacity of jails which is a serious security and health risk and poses a myriad of sanitation problems.
Proposes the establishment of regional penal colonies for the incarceration of convicted prisoners instead of transferring them to the national penitentiaries.
Mandates the Bureau of Corrections to ensure that each prison facility shall strive to adhere to the UN Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners (the Nelson Mandel Rules and other national and international standards.)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2018-08-08

rows.author: I044;I037;I033;C105;I039;
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF COMPUTER LABORATORY IN ALL PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Recognizes the value of computer technology and access to the Internet in enhancing and facilitating learning and education of students in basic education.
Provides that every public elementary and high school shall have at least one room that shall be used as a computer laboratory and mandates DepEd to include in the curriculum of said schools, computer and internet literacy.
rows.alias_name: “Computer and Internet Literacy for Public School Act”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-08-08

rows.author: G101;
rows.title_full: AN ACT SEPARATING THE REGULATORY AND COMMERCIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE PHILIPPINE PORTS AUTHORITY (PPA) BY CONVERTING IT INTO PHILIPPINE PORTS CORPORATION FOR DEVELOPMENT, MANAGEMENT AND OPERATION OF PUBLIC PORTS WITHIN ITS SYSTEM AND TRANSFERRING THE REGULATORY FUNCTIONS TO THE MARITIME INDUSTRY AUTHORITY (MARINA)
rows.abstract:
Addresses the problems of port users (e.g. domestic shippers, exporters and importers) as to low service levels, inefficient port operations and ever-increasing port charges.
Aims to reform the country´s ports administration to avoid conflict of interest arising from regulatory agencies vested with both regulatory and development or commercial functions,
States that Philippine Ports Corporation (PHILPORTS) is a public enterprise, is not primarily a revenue-generating entity but a service provider.  As such, its shall always give utmost priority and importance to public service delivery and promotion of public interest.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2018-08-08

rows.author: G005;F036;G064;G028;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE OROQUIETA AGR0-INDUSTRIAL SCHOOL (OAIS) IN THE CITY OF OROQUIETA, PROVINCE OF MISAMIS OCCIDENTAL, INTO A STATE COLLEGE TO BE KNOWN AS THE MISAMIS OCCIDENTAL STATE COLLEGE (MOSC), REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4941, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Converting The Oroquieta Agr0-industrial School (oais) In The City Of Oroquieta, Province Of Misamis Occidental, Into A State College To Be Known As The Misamis Occidental State College ( M O S C )
rows.status: Republic Act RA11282 enacted on 2019-04-12

rows.author: I105;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING EMERGENCY RICE RESERVES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2018-10-10

rows.author: I105;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL NUCLEAR RADIATION SAFETY BOARD AND DEFINING ITS SCOPE, FUNCTIONS AND POWERS
rows.abstract:
Aims to establish NNRSB that will be responsible for formulating programs, management and provide policies that will aid in the prevention or minimization of nuclear technology risks or threats.
Tasks the Board to regulate all undertakings of nuclear radiation researches, developmental application for the safety and protection of the general public and thereby prevent or decrease the risks which such activities post to life, property and ecology.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2018-08-08

rows.author: I085;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FREE EDUCATION FOR THE CHILDREN AND QUALIFIED DEPENDENTS OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS WHO DIED IN SERVICE
rows.abstract:
Seeks to extend social guarantees to public school teachers and their families by granting educational scholarship to their qualified beneficiaries should they encounter their untimely demise or have been permanently incapacitated while still in service.
Provision of said privileges to these Teacher´s dependent/s commences from the time of their death or permanent incapacity until these students graduate from a four (4) or five (5) year degree in college in any State Universities and Colleges (SUCs).
Also provides for exemption in the payment of any school fees, and a monthly stipend, book and clothing allowance shall be granted to said scholars.
rows.alias_name: “Survivorship Educational Benefit for Public School Teachers´ Dependents Act”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-08-08

rows.author: I085;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STANDARDIZING THE APPROPRIATE CLASS SIZE IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS NATIONWIDE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to ensure that existing school facilities and learning spaces that are used by our young learners are conducive to quality learning.
Seeks to institutionalize an international class size standard of no more than 30 students; considers any class exceeding 30 students up to a maximum of 45 students as LARGE CLASS; and prohibits class size of more than 45 students.
Entitles a teacher handling a large class additional compensation equivalent to five (5%) percent of their daily rate for every student in excess of the standard class size of 30.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-08-08

rows.author: I085;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING CERTAIN WORKING INCENTIVES OF ON-THE-JOB TRAINEE NURSES IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE HOSPITALS, PROHIBITING THE COLLECTION OF EXPERIENCE FEES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to provide certain working incentives for trainee nurses while rendering experiential service to any hospital.
Specifically provides for the rate to compute the incentives which shall not be less that fifty percent (50%) of the minimum daily wage.
Aims to penalize hospitals that demand payment from trainee nurses in exchange for actual nursing experience gained while working in a particular hospital.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: 0095;I091;H040;I030;H017;G083;
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2019-02-04, transmitted to the Senate on 2019-02-06 and received by the Senate on 2019-02-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT THE SEASONABLE FILING OF A MOTION FOR RECONSIDERATION AND/OR APPEAL SHALL STAY THE EXECUTION OF THE CHALLENGED ORDER OF DECISION
rows.abstract:
Intends to unequivocally provide that a seasonable motion for reconsideration, appeal or petition for review shall stay the execution of the challenged order or decision until the rendition of a final judgment affirming the said controverted order or decision.
States that Sec.7 of Rule III of the Rules of Procedure of the Office of the Ombudsman, Sec.65 of Rule 12 of the Revised Rules on Administrative Cases in the Civil Service and similar rules, issuances and statutes are hereby modified or abrogated in so far as they provide that a challenged order of decision is executory pending a motion for reconsideration or appeal.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08870

coauthors.name: CAMPOS, LUIS JOSE ANGEL JR. N.

rows.status: Substituted by HB08179

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY PHILHEALTH COVERAGE OF ALL PERSONS WITH DISABILITY (PWD), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7277, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"MAGNA CARTA FOR PERSONS WITH DISABILITY\"
rows.title_short: Providing For The Mandatory Philhealth Coverage Of All Persons With Disability ( P W D ), Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 7277, As Amended
rows.abstract: Mandates automatic Philhealth coverage of all PWDs not currently afforded health insurance under any existing category. Provides for funding to be sourced from the National Health Insurance Fund of Philhealth earmarked from the proceeds of Republic Act No. 10351.
rows.status: Republic Act RA11228 enacted on 2019-02-22

rows.author: H084;G101;
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING SOLAR PARA SA BAYAN CORPORATION A FRANCHISE TO CONSTRUCT, INSTALL, ESTABLISH, OPERATE AND MAINTAIN DISTRIBUTABLE POWER TECHNOLOGIES AND MINIGRID SYSTEMS THROUGHOUT THE PHILIPPINES TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO SUSTAINABLE ENERGY
rows.status: Substituted by HB08179

rows.author: F123;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA FOR WORKERS, ENTERPRISES AND ORGANIZATIONS IN THE INFORMAL ECONOMY AND PROVIDING MECHANISMS FOR RECOGNITION, INTEGRATION, AND TRANSITION TO THE FORMAL ECONOMY
rows.abstract:
Refers “Informal Economy” to all economic activities by workers and economic units that are, in law or in practice, not covered or insufficiently covered by formal arrangements, and which lack social protection and are subject to hazardous working conditions.
Seeks to provide rights and benefits for workers in the informal economies by giving affordable social protection and security in the workplace.
Also provides for:  labor standards and enforcement of labor laws for its informal workers; creation of Informal Economy Development Council (IEDC); and establishment of Workers in Informal Employment Local Development Office (WIELDO).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE USE OF SIDEWALKS FOR COMMERCIAL AND/OR PERSONAL PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to clear sidewalks and other public spaces from unauthorized commercial or personal use in order to facilitate the smooth passage of persons as well as to clear all obstructions to traffic and vehicular flow.
Specifically enumerates prohibited acts and the corresponding penalties to any person who violates such acts; and holds LGU officials who fail to implement this Act administratively liable and shall be penalized by a fine of P100,000.00 - P500,000.00.
Compels LGUS to formulate a development plan that will make possible an organized vending program for all affected and displaced sidewalk vendors.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENHANCE THE USE OF NATIONAL WEALTH FOR LOCAL DEVELOPMENT BY AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS IN BOOK II OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the funneling of the 80% of the proceeds of LGU energy sources to non-priority projects aimed at lowering their respective community´s electricity consumption costs.  
Amends Sec.294 of the Local Government Code of 1991 to read as follows:
SEC 294. Development and Livelihood Projects. - The proceeds from the share of local government units pursuant to this chapter shall be appropriated by their respective sanggunian to finance local government and livelihood projects IN THE APPROVED LOCAL DEVELOPMENT INVESTMENT PROGRAM AND ANNUAL INVESTMENT PROGRAM.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENHANCE THE SHARE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS IN INTERNAL REVENUE TAXES
rows.abstract: Mandates that local govt units shall have a share in the internal revenue taxes INCLUSIVE OF VALUE ADDED TAX PAID ON IMPORTS to provide the LGUs to pursue economic development and fund programs for improvement of their respective constituents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENHANCE INTER-LGU COOPERATION BY AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS IN BOOK I OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Provides that local government units may group themselves and coordinate their efforts and resources by forming an alliance and obtain legal personality.  Establishes a National Registry of Alliances to register the alliance of LGUs and establish the legal personality and all the consequent implications of the same.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RATIONALIZE CREDIT FINANCING FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS BY AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS IN BOOK II OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Allows Local Government Units to avail of credit facilities to finance local infrastructure and other socio-economic development projects to private capital markets. Ensures that LGUs do not abuse their right to avail of credit lines for the purpose of stabilizing local finances.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR BUSINESS-FRIENDLY TAX REMEDIES IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS BY AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS IN BOOK II OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Provides for the procedure for the approval and effectivity of tax ordinances and revenue measures; and the proceedings required in holding mandatory public hearings. Aims to provide additional measures to ensure the observance of procedural due process in the exercise of remedies for taxpayers, particularly in disputing tax assessments and in filing of claims for refund.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENHANCE THE TAXING POWERS OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS BY AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS IN BOOK II OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Aims to increase the annual fixed tax rate for delivery trucks or vans of manufacturers or producers from P500 to P1,500;  reduce the taxable base of the head office from 30 % to 10 % of gross sales or revenues; increase the share of sales outlets and the likes from 70% to 90%; remove the authority of the national government to provides exemptions on local taxes, fees and charges;  and limit LGUs to provide local exemptions from taxes, fees and charges.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENHANCE PUBLIC FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS BY AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS IN REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Mandates the Department of Local Government (DILG), Department of Finance (DOF), Department of Budget and Management (DBM), and the National Economic Development Authority (NEDA) to provide guidance to local government units regarding public financial management. Highlights the oversight role of the Provincial, City, and Municipal governments to ensure that provinces, cities, municipalities and barangays adhere to the principles and policies of good governance and efficient public financial management.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PROHIBITING POLITICAL DYNASTIES, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Defines “Political Dynasty” as the concentration, consolidation, or perpetuation of public office and political powers by relatives within the 2nd degree of consanguinity or affinity.
Provides prohibited candidates and covered scenarios in the application of this Act to the next elections and all subsequent elections thereafter.
Allows the COMELEC to deny, motu proprio, and/or cancel certificate of candidacy of any candidate/party if it becomes apparent from the documents filed that a violation of this Act may have been committed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 5 AND 8 OF REPUBLIC ACT (RA) NO. 9505, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PERSONAL EQUITY AND RETIREMENT ACCOUNT (PERA) LAW AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Increases the annual Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA) contributions entitled to tax incentives from P100,000 to 200,000 or up to P400,000 for OFWs. Provides that instead of a 5% tax credit, PERA contributions up to the maximum amount shall be allowed as deductions from gross income tax of each contributor.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN THE INTERNAL AFFAIRS SERVICE OF THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975 AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8551, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to strengthen the Internal Affairs Service  (IAS) of the PNP to make them more effective and efficient in promoting higher standards of integrity in the police force. Provides integrity development functions such as character building, lifestyle checks and investigation and impose restrictions, file appropriate criminal cases against PNP members before the regular courts and assist in the prosecution of cases. 
Grants IAS to formulate and adopt its own disciplinary rules and mechanisms and fiscal independence that shall be distinct and separate from the PNP.
Provides that the police internal affairs investigation shall be finished within 30 days after criminal charges had been filed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE YOUTH DRUG ABUSE RESISTANCE EDUCATION AND PREVENTION PROGRAM AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Mandates the Department of Health, in close coordination with Department of Education (DepEd), Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and other appropriate agencies, to administer, coordinate and recommend policies to avoid opportunities of drug abuse and live drug-free lives of the youth. The Y-DARE shall also include livelihood and training programs to provide the youth with appropriate skills to prevent them from falling victim to illegal drugs.
rows.alias_name: “Youth Drug Abuse Resistance Education and Prevention Program (Y-DARE) ACT OF 2018”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2019-01-23

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A NATIONAL COMPREHENSIVE FRAMEWORK ON RESILIENT HOUSING AND HUMAN SETTLEMENTS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Provides for a framework  for the creation of livable, safe, resilient, sustainable and pro-poor housing and human settlements that is structurally designed to resist or absorb the effects of climate hazards.
rows.alias_name: “Resilient Housing and Human Settlements Act of 2018.”
rows.status: Tabled by the Committee on 2019-01-23

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE BARANGAY UNIT THROUGH SUPPORT FOR BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND BARANGAY VOLUNTEER WORKERS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Grants barangay health workers and barangay tanods monthly honorarium of Five Hundred (P500) pesos. In addition to financial benefits, they shall also be provided with training and workshops to effectively exercise their duty, PhilHealth coverage and free legal services.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF THE DEFINITION OF THE CRIME OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT TO INCLUDE UNWANTED TEXT MESSAGES, ELECTRONIC MAIL OR COMMUNICATIONS, OR OTHER SIMILAR MEANS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-EIGHT HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"SEXUAL HARASSMENT LAW\"
rows.abstract: Amends Sec. 3 of RA 7877 by expanding the definition of sexual harassment acts to include sending SMS messages, electronic mail, internet chat and other similar means of conveying messages via electronic communication that constitute sexual harassment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY OF THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN BY AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6770, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE OMBUDSMAN ACT OF 1989\", AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Seeks to broaden the investigative and prosecutorial powers of the Ombudsman by allowing them the following: employ wiretapping as an investigation technique after a grant of judicial authority; to issue subpoena and subpoena duces tecum to compel and secure the compulsory attendance of any witness or the production of evidence; the power to examine and access bank and non-bank accounts and transactions; and the power to punish for contempt.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO IMPROVE AND TO PROMOTE QUALITY DELIVERY OF HEALTH SERVICES IN BARANGAYS, ENACTING THE \"BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS AND SERVICES REFORM ACT OF 2018\"
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish one Barangay Health Center in every barangay unit which shall be composed of Nurses, Midwife and Barangay Health Worker.
Provides that barangay health workers shall receive an entry pay level equivalent to Salary Grade One “SG 1” and shall be entitled to the same incentives and benefits provided under the Magna Carta for Public Health Workers.   Further, they shall be covered by the existing statutory benefits such as GSIS, Philhealth, and Pag-ibig.
rows.alias_name: “Barangay Health Workers and Services Reform Act of 2018.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A STRATEGIC FOOD SECURITY RICE RESERVE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Mandates the National Food Authority (NFA) to maintain rice reserve equivalent to fifteen (15) days of national rice consumption, buy stocks from small farmers and their cooperatives and import only under abnormal conditions, and release them to the market upon declaration of a state of calamity.
Strengthens farmers´ cooperatives by mandating the Cooperative Development Authority in coordination with the LGUs and NGOs to transform agri-based cooperatives into entrepreneurs.
rows.alias_name: “Strategic Food Security Rice Reserve Act of 2018.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2018-10-10

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT CURTAILING THE ILLEGAL ACTIVITIES OF RACKETEERS AND POWERFUL SYNDICATES IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Declares it unlawful for any person to a.) knowingly participate with or in an enterprise conducting a pattern of racketeering activity; b.) received any money derived from a pattern of a racketeering activity, or act as a dummy of any person in order to conceal money or property; c.) use or invest any part of the money or property received from a pattern of racketeering activity in any interest in or control of any business enterprise; d.) acquire or maintain through a pattern of racketeering activity any interest in or control of any business or enterprise; and e.) conspire in the conduct of any unlawful acts provided in this Act. 
Provides that all rights, titles and interest in property acquired, maintained or derived through racketeering activity shall be vested in the Philippines government upon the commission of the act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ACCELERATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF IDLE AND UNDERUTILIZED AGRICULTURAL LANDS AS MEANS TO GENERATE EMPLOYMENT
rows.abstract: Aims to utilize idle or underutilized lands by converting one million hectares of public lands into modern productive agricultural resources planted with hybrid corn, cassava, and other high value crops, thereby creating at least one million jobs and annual farm incomes of at least Twenty Five Thousand Pesos.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE EMPLOYMENT RIGHTS FOR MEMBERS OF THE CITIZEN ARMED FORCES FOR THE RESERVED FORCE OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Aims to protect military reservist from discrimination in job hiring, reintegration, promotion, or any employment benefits. Ensures reservists proper training and compensation and guarantees those injured or disabled during their service reintegration to the civilian work force .
rows.status: Consolidated into HB07421

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DEMOCRATIZATION OF PUBLIC SCHOOL EDUCATION
rows.abstract:
Declares it unlawful for any public school official to refuse admission of any student in primary or secondary public school where the student is a bona fide resident of the community.
Penalizes public school official or employee who violates any provisions of this Act with one (1) month suspension from service and Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) fine for the first offense, dismissal from service and temporary disqualification to hold public office for six (6) months for the second offense, and dismissal from service and perpetual disqualification to hold public office for third or subsequent offenses.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR PUBLIC SALE SHARES IN THE DISPOSITION OF GOVERNMENT CORPORATIONS UNDER THE PRIVATIZATION PROGRAM
rows.abstract: Provides that whenever government owned or controlled corporation or any of their assets are privatized, it shall be through a public offering of not less that 60 % of its shares of stock ; and no person shall own more than 5 % of the  shares of stock of the corporation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REQUIRE HOSPITALS TO ESTABLISH AND IMPLEMENT SECURITY PROCEDURES TO REDUCE THE LIKELIHOOD OF INFANT PATIENT ABDUCTION AND BABY SWITCHING, INCLUDING PROCEDURES FOR IDENTIFYING ALL INFANT PATIENTS IN THE HOSPITAL IN A MANNER THAT ENSURES IT WILL BE EVIDENT IF INFANTS ARE MISSING FROM THE HOSPITAL
rows.abstract:
Provides that all hospitals, public or private, shall keep an identification record of all newborn infants under their care and to ensure that such records shall prevent infant abduction or baby switching.
Identification record shall include any of the following: the footprint, fingerprint or photograph of the infant; written description of the infant; and an identification bracelet or anklet put on the newborn patient.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE TYPOLOGY OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2018-08-08

rows.author: H064;
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE CREATION OF THE POSITION OF THE MUNICIPAL GENERAL SERVICES OFFICER, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE BOOK III, TITLE TWO, CHAPTER 2, SECTION 443 (a) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PERSONNEL OF BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENTS, MEMBERS OF ORGANIZATIONS OR ASSOCIATIONS AND ALL OTHER PERSONS PROVIDING TOURISM SERVICES TO UNDERGO BASIC FIRST AID TRAINING
rows.abstract:
Mandates all personnel of business establishments, members of organizations or associations providing tourism services to undergo basic first aid training by the Philippine National Red Cross and other reputable organizations or institutions providing such training who shall issue the necessary certifications for this purpose.

Ensures the safety of tourists by requiring such establishments to be equipped with first aid kits that the local government units shall inspect on a periodic or regular basis.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING CORPORATE FARMING AND PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Establishes a  national corporate farming program where corporations or partnerships, through direct ownership or lease of farmland, may engage in the agricultural production of rice and corn.

Provides an incentive package which exempts the corporations or partnerships participating in the corporate farming program from paying certain taxes. Loans extended by banks to said participating corporations or partnerships shall be treated as compliance with RA10000 or “The Agri-Agra Reform Credit Act of 2009.”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2018-08-14

rows.abstract: Aims to protect the intellectual property rights of Indigenous Cultural Communities and Indigenous Peoples in their promotion in mainstream mass media, specifically the movie and television industry.  Provides measures and minimum standards to be met by movie and television enterprises in portraying and/or representing these cultural communities to safeguard their cultural identity and heritage.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2018-08-14

rows.abstract: Aims to remove the restrictions under Sections 118, 119 and 121 of Commonwealth Act No. 141 regarding the registration, acquisition, encumbrance, alienation, transfer and conveyance of land covered by agricultural free patent. Provides that agricultural free patents shall be considered as titles in fee simple and shall not be subject to any restrictions.

rows.abstract:
Aims to reconstitute the PCA Board that shall manage the Coconut Farmers and Industry Development Trust Fund.
Authorizes the PCA to implement a reorganization plan to increase its personnel complement with a dedicated unit for planning, evaluation of proposals and monitoring of the proposals and projects funded by the Coconut Farmers and Industry Development Trust Fund.

rows.title_full: THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENT CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Aims to establish a market-responsive, globally competitive, stable, transparent, time-bound and performance-based investment regime and integrated investment promotion programs and strategies. 
Addresses the regulation of investments and administration of incentives and promotion and facilitation functions required of the established and existing Investment Promotion Agencies.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF FULLY-EQUIPPED SCIENCE LABORATORIES IN EVERY PUBLIC ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOL AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Provides infrastructure projects for the upgrade, maintenance and development of laboratory rooms and facilities in all elementary and secondary schools. 
Gives tax incentives to private entities engaging in S&T development; 20% tax deduction from the total revenue obligations for private schools who shall import laboratory equipment/facilities for the exclusive use in their school; 3% tax incentive from the importation of raw materials for private entities engaged in the manufacture of laboratory equipment needed in public schools.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2018-08-14

rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING ELECTRICITY RATES BY ALLOCATING THE NET NATIONAL GOVERNMENT SHARE FROM THE MALAMPAYA NATURAL GAS PROJECT FOR THE PAYMENT OF THE STRANDED CONTRACT COSTS AND STRANDED DEBTS OF THE NATIONAL POWER CORPORATION
rows.abstract: Seeks to lower power costs by using the net national government share from the Malampaya Fund solely for the payment of NPC´s Stranded Contract Costs and Stranded Debts which shall be remitted to a Special Trust Fund to be administered by the PSALM. The amounts allocated shall be included in the General Appropriations Act and the DBM shall provide a timely release of the amounts allocated and appropriated in accordance with its debt and independent power producer payment schedule.

rows.author: I091;I112;
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING  14TH MONTH PAY FOR ALL EMPLOYEES IN THE GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE SECTOR REGARDLESS OF STATUS OF EMPLOYMENT
rows.abstract: Sets schedules for the released of the 13th month pay on or before May 31; and 14th month pay on or before November 30 every year. Provides that for employees employed for less than one (1) year, their 14th month pay shall be prorated to the number of months served. Exempts the 14th month pay from the computation of the employee´s gross income provided, that it shall not exceed ninety thousand pesos (P90,000.00).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2018-08-15
